title: legjobb and egyformán: The Best, or Equally Good

sections.title: When there's a winner, and when there isn't
sections.content: You already form a superlative with leg- + comparative: legjobb, legérdekesebb. It works just as well picking a winner among three or more things you're comparing, not just hotel rooms. But sometimes there isn't a winner — you already know egyforma ("the same, identical"); add the -n/-an/-en ending you use for manner adverbs (gyorsan, lassan) and you get egyformán ("equally, the same way"), for when two things are simply tied.

sections.title: Picking a winner, or not
rows: Ez a legjobb film, amit láttam.
This is the best film I've seen.
The two restaurants are equally good.

items.spanish: Szerintem ez a legszebb város Magyarországon.
items.english: In my opinion, this is the most beautiful city in Hungary.
Both are good books, I liked them equally.

sections.content: mindkettő ("both, both of them") is the natural subject for egyformán — Mindkettő jó, de egyformán jó lets you say two things are both good, and equally so, in one short pair of sentences.
